descriptionChirho: Nifal: to be turned back, retreat, or withdraw, often in a military or physical sense of being driven back or falling back.
To turn back from loyalty or faithfulness, especially from God; to backslide or apostatize, used both as a participle (the backslider) and in vows of fidelity.
Qal: to turn aside or deviate from the right path, emphasizing moral or directional straying rather than retreat.
